q: Which prompt contains all four parts of the framework: role, context, task and format?
options: 'You are my executive assistant. The client is upset about a late delivery. Draft a short apology email, warm but professional, under 100 words.'
explanation: It names the role (executive assistant), the context (an upset client, a late delivery), the task (draft an apology email) and the format (short, warm but professional, under 100 words). The others leave the AI guessing.

q: Which two of the four parts are still missing from this prompt: 'Summarise our Q3 sales results in five bullet points'?
explanation: It has the task (summarise) and the format (five bullet points), but no role for the AI to play and no context — no audience, background or constraints to shape the answer.

q: AI's first draft of your email is far too formal for your client. What is the best next move?
options: Start over with a completely new prompt
Follow up: 'Make this friendlier and less formal'
Accept the draft — you only get one attempt
Silently edit it in Word and never mention it again
explanation: Your first answer is a draft, not a verdict. Editing beats restarting every time, so follow up with adjustments like 'make it shorter' or 'more direct' until it fits.
